subject: Clarify: SLO measurement windows, alerts, and dashboard access for inference endpoints
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@techhaven.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@techhaven.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:02:15-07:00
Subject: SLO measurement and exception handling for inference endpoints

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — the performance looked promising. Procurement asked me to confirm a few specifics about how Redwood measures SLOs for "inference endpoints" before we move to legal. High-level items we need answers to for our questionnaire: 

1) Latency definition: Is p99 measured end-to-end (client request -> final token sent) or only within the server processing window? Do retries/cold starts get included?
2) Measurement windows: Do you use rolling windows (e.g., 1m, 5m, 1h) or calendar-aligned windows for SLO assessment? How is monthly uptime computed?
3) Alerting: What thresholds trigger proactive alerts to the customer vs internal ops? Can we integrate Redwood alerts into our PagerDuty?
4) Dashboard & evidence: Can TechHaven get read-only access to the same Grafana dashboards you use for SLO monitoring? If not, what evidence do you provide during procurement?
5) Exception process: If we request an SLA exception for a short-term traffic pattern (e.g., black Friday burst), what's the review/approval flow and typical lead time?

If you have a short PDF spec or a one-page cheat sheet (latency formulas, sampling window, measurement exclusions), that would be ideal to attach to our internal questionnaire. We are working toward a mid-November start date, so a quick turnaround on this would help.

Best,
Alex Morgan
Sr. Procurement Manager, TechHaven
procurement@techhaven.com

Attachments: none

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@techhaven.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T13:18:03-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO measurement and exception handling for inference endpoints

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. I'll answer each item at a high level here and attach a short spec that lays out exact formulas and the reporting artifacts we provide. Connor (serving runtime) and Marissa (customer success/ops) are cc'd for any deeper technical or operational follow-ups.

Summary answers (details in attached slo-metric-spec-v1.pdf):

1) Latency definition:
- p99/p95 are measured end-to-end from the time the request is received by the Redwood ingress to the time the final token is emitted to the client (so includes all server-side processing).
- Cold starts are excluded from standard SLO calculations by default; we track a separate cold-start metric and can include them if customers request that in their contract.
- Retries: automatic retry attempts performed by Redwood's client libraries are excluded from latency computations; customer-initiated retries are included.

2) Measurement windows:
- We compute rolling percentiles over multiple windows: 1m, 5m, 1h for alerting and a 30d rolling window for monthly SLO evaluation. Monthly uptime is computed as 1 - (total downtime_seconds / total_seconds_in_month), where downtime is measured against our successful response criteria defined in the spec.
- For contracts that require calendar-month reports instead of rolling windows, we can provide calendar-aligned aggregates.

3) Alerting and integrations:
- Default alert tiers: 1m p99 degradations (informational), sustained 5m p99 degradations (actionable), and 1h service errors rate spike (escalation). Thresholds are configurable per-customer.
- Yes — we support webhook-based alert forwarding and a direct PagerDuty integration for enterprise customers. Alerts can be mapped to customer escalation policies.

4) Dashboards & evidence:
- We provide read-only Grafana access scoped to the customer's account (SSO + time-limited tokens). For procurement, we can also provide an export bundle (CSV/PNG) and a monthly SLO report PDF.

5) Exception process:
- Short-term exceptions (performance accommodations for predictable traffic bursts) are handled by the account team + infra ops. Typical workflow: request -> impact analysis (24-72h) -> provisional exception (yes/no) -> documented terms (duration, additional costs, any SLO adjustments). For long-term exceptions we follow a formal amendment path through legal.

Attached: slo-metric-spec-v1.pdf (contains formulas, excluded event types, synthetic probe design, and evidence examples). Connor and Marissa — please weigh in if I've missed anything operationally.

Thanks,
Mina
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-metric-spec-v1.pdf (spec, 3 pages)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@techhaven.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@techhaven.com
Date: 2026-10-12T08:47:25-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO measurement and exception handling for inference endpoints

Mina — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple follow-ups from procurement & our platform team before we finalize the questionnaire: 

A) Cold-starts: if they are excluded by default, can you provide the cold-start rate and its distribution (p50/p95/p99) for the last 30 days for our prospective region? We need that for risk assessment.

B) Downtime definition: you mentioned "successful response criteria" — does that exclude 4xx responses initiated by the caller (e.g., malformed prompts)? We want to be sure penalties/credits only apply to Redwood service failures.

C) Dashboard access: read-only Grafana is ideal. Is the access via SAML SSO? If possible we'd prefer short-lived SSO invites tied to our procurement reviewers rather than creating permanent accounts.

D) Exception SLAs: can you confirm typical lead time for a provisional exception if we request it one week before a runway event? Procurement needs to know whether the 24-72h analysis window you mention is realistic for last-minute marketing spikes.

If you can attach an anonymized 30-day cold-start distribution snapshot and a sample Grafana invite (or steps to request one), that will get us across the finish line.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are aiming to issue a PO in the coming weeks.

Best,
Alex

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@techhaven.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO measurement and exception handling for inference endpoints

Alex — quick update and attachments to close the open items. See inline: 

A) Cold-starts: attached is an anonymized snapshot (30d) showing cold-start rate and p50/p95/p99 for the US-west region. Those numbers are computed from synthetic and production traces and labeled in the attachment. Note: cold starts have fallen after recent runtime optimizations; we exclude them from the contractual SLO by default but will include them on request.

B) Downtime / successful responses: our definition excludes caller-induced 4xx errors and client-side timeouts. The SLO applies to Redwood service failures (5xx, infrastructure connectivity failures, or internal processor errors). The spec has the precise status-code buckets and examples.

C) Grafana access: we issue time-limited read-only SSO invites via your IdP (SAML/OIDC). For procurement reviewers we can create 14-day invites scope-limited to SLO dashboards; sample invite content is attached as grafana-readonly-invite.txt. To proceed we need a name + email and the SAML entity id for your IdP; instructions are in the attached file.

D) Exception timing: for predictable events (e.g., marketing campaigns) if you submit the request >=72 hours before the event we can typically finalize a provisional exception (yes/no and suggested config) within that 24-72h window. Requests with <72h lead time can still be evaluated, but operational constraints may require temporary mitigations (rate limiting, prioritized routing) instead of formal exceptions. If you need ultra-fast turnarounds we can offer a paid expedited review.

Attached: slo-metric-spec-v1.pdf, anonymized-cold-starts-30d.csv (referenced inside the spec), grafana-readonly-invite.txt, monthly-uptime-credit-calculator.xlsx

Next steps: I'll upload the Grafana invite once you confirm the reviewer identities and IdP metadata, and I'll ask Connor to run the region-specific cold-start extraction if you want a different region or a longer history. Marissa will open a procurement ticket in our portal that cross-links the sample contract language for the exception clause so legal can see it.

If you'd like, we can hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through the spec and Grafana.

Thanks,
Mina
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
